evals.prompt: Here are three reference images. Make our site illustrations look like these, but don't attach them to every render.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads every reference, writes the JSON prompt fields (task, style, frame) and the subject shape in concrete plain sentences, proves them by rendering 4-6 unrelated subjects with no images attached and identical params, compares a sheet against the references, iterates one change per numbered round, and freezes the style file as JSON on approval.
assertions: Writes every prompt as a JSON specification, not prose blocks
Writes task, style and frame fields with a flat hex frame.background, plus the subject object shape
Uses vivid colour names, full plain sentences and concrete descriptions instead of keyword lists or genre labels
Describes nothing from the references' own contents
Renders 4-6 unrelated subjects with no images attached and identical params
Builds a sheet with the references beside the renders and reads it
Changes one thing per round and keeps numbered versions
Writes art/styles/<style>.json with model, params, task, style, frame, banned words, and traps on approval

evals.prompt: Like this one (points at a glossy 3D render of a chess set). Make our icons and the big hero illustrations in that style.
evals.expected_output: The agent settles which trait the user means, such as the glossy finish, rather than copying chess pieces, and writes one style file with a scales entry for icons and one for illustrations.
assertions: Asks or infers which trait of the reference to take instead of copying its objects
Keeps chess pieces out of the style and frame fields
Adds scales for icons (one object, bold silhouette, no small detail) and illustrations, each with its own readability, framing, aspect ratio and resolution
Keeps one shared style object for both

evals.prompt: We already have 20 images in the frozen 'paper' style. Tweak the style to make the colours warmer.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not reword the existing style file. It creates a new version, proves it, and tells the user existing images must be re-rendered or stay on the old version.
assertions: Does not edit the frozen style in place
Creates a new numbered version of the style
Tells the user the existing images are re-rendered or stay on the old version
Writes the new version as a separate art/styles JSON file and leaves the frozen one's sentences unchanged
